FOOD.tip: Lean chicken with no skin and no bones. Gravy and fatty leftovers upset a dog's tummy, so they stay on the people plates.
FOOD.note: +30 Hunger, +10 Happiness. Chicken, carrot and green beans, cooked soft.

FOOD.tip: Plain mashed sweet potato, no sugar and no chestnut syrup. Mochi never goes in a dog's bowl, it is far too sticky to swallow safely.
FOOD.note: +15 Hunger, +15 Happiness. Golden sweet potato mash, for a lucky year.

FOOD.tip: Carrot and apple, cut small, with the core and every seed taken out. Apple seeds are not safe for dogs, so not one goes in the bag.

FOOD.tip: Plain cooked turkey with no skin, bones, gravy or seasoning, and just a few fresh cranberries. Cranberry sauce is full of sugar, so only the fresh berries go in.

Giant Crayon Box.story: Every crayon is taller than a dog. Nobody has ever finished colouring.

Family Photo Frame.story: Everyone who ever shared this yard is on the fence. The ugly ones are the best.

Doggy Ramp.story: Paw prints lead all the way up. Nobody has needed the ramp yet, but everyone is proud of it.

Rocking Chair.story: A dog-sized chair with a knitted blanket. Mum likes a rock here after a long day of puppies.

Jack-o-Lantern Trio.story: Three pumpkins, three faces, all of them smiling. They glow a little after dark.

Paper Bat Bunting.story: Paper bats on a string, cut a bit wonky. They flutter whenever a dog runs past.

Friendly Scarecrow.story: A pumpkin head and a big grin. The crows sit on his arms to chat.

Pumpkin Lantern.story: A round pumpkin lantern on a little post. It glows softly after dark.

Ghost Garland.story: Little cloth ghosts holding hands. They say boo very quietly.

Ghost Lantern String.story: Little paper ghost lanterns on a string. After dark they glow softly, and each one smiles.

Pumpkin Fairy Lights.story: Tiny pumpkin bulbs on a green wire. They light up the fence when the sun goes down.

Friendly Fence Web.story: A wobbly crayon web with a round little spider in a bow. She waves at every dog who passes.

Cardboard Black Cat.story: A cardboard cat painted black, with a big smile. The dogs sniff it every morning, just in case.

Cauldron Planter.story: A black pot on stubby legs, full of sunflowers and pansies. Both are safe for dogs to sniff.

Felt Fir Tree.story: A soft felt fir in a pot, hung with paper stars the size of a paw. Felt, because real fir needles can upset a dog's tummy.

Yard Snowman.story: Lumpy, a bit lopsided, with a carrot nose and a knitted scarf. He waves with his longer arm.

Candy-Cane Fairy Lights.story: Red-and-white striped bulbs on a green wire. After dark the fence looks like a row of sweets.

Present Pile.story: Three wrapped boxes with big bows. They are empty, but every dog checks, every single day.

Star Lantern.story: A paper star on a wooden post, with little holes cut in it. After dark it glows and puts stars on the snow.

Bird Bath.story: A stone bowl on a pedestal for the garden birds. The sparrows splash in it every morning and the dogs watch, very politely.

Flower Barrel.story: An old wooden barrel full of sunflowers and snapdragons. Both are safe for dogs, who sniff every single one.

String Lights.story: Little round bulbs on a long wire. They come on by themselves when it gets dark, which looks like magic but is a timer.

Garden Bench.story: A painted wooden bench with room for one person and three dogs. The dogs always get the good end.

Hammock.story: A striped hammock between two posts. It swings in the breeze and nobody has ever got out of it gracefully.

Wind Chime.story: Bamboo tubes and a little wooden bird that clink in the breeze. The dogs tilt their heads at every note.

Sandbox.story: A wooden box of soft sand with a little spade. The one place in the yard where digging gets a round of applause.

Stepping Stones.story: Five flat stones in a wobbly line across the grass. Every dog hops them in a different order.

Braided Rag Rug.story: A round rug braided from old shirts and one sock. It is the warmest spot on the floor at four o'clock.

Toy Basket.story: A wicker basket of squeaky friends. Every toy comes out and not one of them ever goes back in.

Cushion Pile.story: Six squashy cushions in a heap. Officially for people, unofficially for dogs.

Boston Fern.story: A big leafy fern on a little wooden stand. Boston ferns are safe around dogs, which is why this one was picked.

Cuckoo Clock.story: A carved wooden clock with a little bird inside. On the hour it pops out, and every dog in the house answers it.

Paw Print Pictures.story: Three little frames, each with one muddy paw print. The artists signed them by sitting on them.

Moon Lamp.story: A round paper moon on a little wooden stand. It glows after dark, so nobody trips over a sleeping dog.

Patchwork Quilt.story: A quilt hung on the wall, one square for every dog who ever lived here. There is plenty of room for more squares.

Dog Play Tower.story: Three carpet steps, a cubby hole and a rope to bat. The top step belongs to whoever got there first.

Tunnel Sofa.story: A squashy little sofa with a tunnel straight through the middle. Dogs go in one end and come out the other, very pleased with themselves.

Ball Pit.story: A soft round pit full of bright balls. Jumping in is allowed, and so is lying very still.

Sofa Ramp.story: A carpeted ramp up to a cushioned top step. Short legs, long backs and old knees all get up without a jump.

Window Seat.story: A cushioned seat under a little round window. The best place in the house to watch the postman and the birds.

Paper Snowflake Garland.story: Paper snowflakes cut by the Nguyen kids, no two the same. Some of them are dogs, if you squint.

Felt Holly Wreath.story: A round wreath of felt leaves and red felt berries. Real holly berries make dogs ill, so these ones are felt.

Red Wooden Sled.story: A red sled for leaning on the fence. Nobody has ever pulled it, because a dog is always sitting in it.

Kadomatsu Pair.story: Bamboo, pine and plum by the gate to welcome the new year's luck. The dogs sniff it every morning to check the luck is still there.

Lucky Cat.story: A white maneki-neko with one paw raised to wave good luck in. The dogs wave back, in their own way.

tools.desc: A pocket gadget that reads coat genes. Free sniffs at the Vet and on the Playdate Board.
